title: Arrumando a mochila
grammar: My e your para dizer de quem é
reading: I pack my bag for class.
My backpack is on the desk.
My notebook is in the backpack.
My pencil and my pen are in the bag.
My sister is here, and my brother is here too.
My name is on my notebook.
dialogue: Excuse me, Tom. Is this your backpack on the desk?
Yes, it is. Thank you! My notebook is in it.
And is this your pencil? It is on the floor.
No, it isn't. My pencil is in my bag.
I see. My name is Lia. This is my sister, Mia.
Nice to meet you, Lia. Is Mia a friend from school?
Yes, she is. She is my sister and my friend too.
Great! Thank you for the help, Lia.

title: Comprando uma passagem só de ida
grammar: One como quantidade explícita
reading: Ben is at the train station today.
He is at the ticket counter with a coffee.
The backpack is on the floor.
A one-way ticket is ten dollars.
The train is at nine in the morning.
Ben is tired, but he is happy.
dialogue: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes. Can I have one ticket to Boston, please?
Sure. One-way or round trip?
One-way, please. Is the train at nine?
Yes, it is. A ticket is twenty dollars.
Okay. Here is the money. I am tired today.
Here you are. Is this your backpack on the floor?
Yes, it is. Thank you! I am happy today.

title: Conferindo o bilhete impresso
grammar: This e these ao mostrar itens próximos
reading: Emma is at the train station with a coffee to go.
These are two printed tickets.
This ticket is for today.
The other ticket is for tomorrow.
The seat number is three.
Both tickets are in the small pocket.
dialogue: Good morning. Are these your tickets?
Yes, they are. Can I check the date with you?
Sure. This ticket is for today, and the other is for tomorrow.
Great. Is the seat number on the ticket?
Yes, it is. Look at this small number.
I see it. Are both tickets one-way?
Yes, both are one-way. Here are your tickets.
Perfect. Two tickets are in my pocket. Thank you!

title: A espera na biblioteca
grammar: There is para apontar um lugar disponível
reading: I am Tom, and I am at the library.
A quiet reading room is on the first floor.
A big table is by the window.
There is one seat at the table.
I have a book and a glass of water.
Now I can read in the quiet room.
dialogue: Excuse me, I have a quick question about the library.
Sure. Is it about a book?
No. I would like a quiet seat to read.
There is a seat at the big table.
Really? Is the table in the reading room?
Yes, it is. There is a window there too.
Great. Can I take my glass of water?
Yes, you can. Please have a seat.

title: Perguntando sobre um parque
grammar: Is there…? para perguntar se existe um lugar
reading: Today is my birthday, and I am in a new town.
I would like a small party in a park.
There is a park near here, on a quiet street.
There is a green gate at the entrance.
The gate is not far, so I go there with my dog.
Now I sit at my party with some water.
dialogue: Excuse me, is there a park near here?
Yes, there is. It is on Green Street.
Is it far? I have my dog with me.
No, it isn't. It is a quick walk.
Great. Is there an entrance on this street?
Yes, there is a green gate on the corner.
Thank you. Today is my birthday, so I have a party there.
Happy birthday! Yes, you can have a party there.

title: Onde eu moro
grammar: In, near e on para situar a moradia
reading: My name is Lia, and I live in a small town.
I live near the sea, in a quiet neighborhood.
My house is on Oak Street.
My mother and father live in the house with me.
There is a park near my house.
On Saturday, I sit in the park and see the sea.
dialogue: Hi Lia. Where is your house?
It is on Oak Street, in a small town.
Nice. Is your neighborhood near the sea?
Yes, it is. I live near the sea and a park.
Really? Is there a place to sit near your house?
Yes, there is. My mother and father are in the park on Saturday.
Great. Can I sit with you on Saturday?
Sure, you can. I am at the park gate on Saturday.

title: À beira do lago
grammar: Next to, by e across from para indicar posição
reading: I am Sam, and Jo is my sister.
We are in the park, by a pond.
The path is next to the pond.
There is a bench by the water, across from a tree.
My brother is on the path, near the sign.
We take a seat on the bench, and it is quiet.
dialogue: Sam, where is the path to the gate?
It is next to the pond, near the entrance.
Is there a bench near the pond?
Yes, there is. It is across from the big tree.
Nice. And where is Tom? Is he near the sign?
No, he is with the duck at the pond.
Great. Is the bench free for me and Tom?
Yes, it is. We can sit on the bench by the water.

title: Escolhendo o lugar de sentar
grammar: A pergunta Where can I sit?
reading: My family and I are at a small restaurant on Main Street.
I would like a window seat, please.
There is an empty table by the window.
A server is at the door, and I ask, 'Where can I sit?'
The restaurant is quiet, and there is a menu on the table.
I take a chair, and my family and I sit.
dialogue: Hi. Where can I sit with my family?
You can sit at the empty table by the door.
Can I have a window seat, please?
Sure. This table is by the window. Here you are.
Thank you. Where can I put my bag?
You can put it on the chair next to you.
Great. Can I have the menu and some water?
Yes, of course. Here is a menu and a glass of water.

title: Escrevendo o nome no papel
grammar: Imperativo de instrução com please
reading: I am Rosa, and I am on a chair at my desk.
There is a sheet of paper on my desk.
I have a blue pen and a name tag.
The teacher is nice: Write your name, please.
I write my name on the line at the top of the page.
Then I put the paper on the empty table.
dialogue: Excuse me, where can I sit and write my name?
Write your name at the top of the page, please.
Can I use my blue pen for the name?
Yes, you can. The blue pen is good.
Can I write my last name too?
Yes. Write both names on the line, please.
Great. Can I put the paper on the empty table?
Yes, you can. Put it there, please.

title: Uma instrução de segurança no trajeto
grammar: Imperativo negativo com do not
reading: My friends and I walk on a trail.
There is a sign near a bridge.
The sign is red and big: Stay on the path.
The bridge is wet, so we do not run.
We are happy, but we are tired.
We take a seat on a bench by the water.
dialogue: Can we run across the bridge, Mia?
No. Do not run on the wet bridge.
Okay. Can we leave the trail here?
No. Stay on the path, please.
Is there a sign by the fence?
Yes, there is. Do not go near the fence.
Okay. I am tired, but I am happy.
Me too. We can sit on a bench by the water.

title: Descrevendo a cidade à beira-mar
grammar: Adjetivo antes do substantivo
reading: I am Alex, and I am in a small seaside town.
The town is on the coast, near a big beach.
The street is quiet in the morning.
I see white houses and a small café.
There is a café with a coastal view.
I am hungry, so I take a chair at the café.
dialogue: What kind of place is this, Alex?
It is a small seaside town on the coast.
Is the street busy, or is it quiet?
It is quiet. There are white houses on the street.
Nice. I am hungry. Is there a café near here?
Yes, there is a café with a coastal view.
Great. Can we sit at a table near the path?
Yes, we can. I see an empty table there, and it is free.

title: Marcando a saída do trem
grammar: At em horários exatos
reading: Ana is at the station.
There is a small departure board on the wall.
The schedule is on the board.
There are three trains this morning.
The old train is at seven.
Ana is on time.
dialogue: Excuse me, where is the departure board for Boston?
It is over there. Go straight, then turn left at the sign.
Thank you. Is there a train to Boston this morning?
Yes, there is. Do not leave your bag here, and look at the schedule.
I see three trains. Is the first one on time?
Yes, it is. The first train is at seven.
Great! Is there another train for the afternoon?
Yes, there is one train at three.

title: Escolhendo uma hora para se encontrar
grammar: What time para pedir um horário
reading: Zoe is at the bus stop.
It is a cold day, and the town is small.
There is a new clock by the sign.
It is noon, and Max is on time.
Zoe and Max are friends.
The bus is at half past six, so they go for a coffee.
dialogue: Hi, Max! It is cold today. What time is it?
Hi, Zoe. Look at the new clock by the sign. It is noon.
Great, we are on time. What time is the bus to the station?
It is at half past six. That is a long way from now.
Really? That is late. What time is the next bus?
The next bus is at two. There is a small schedule on the sign.
Perfect! I would like a hot coffee, please.
Sure, no problem. Two coffees, and then the bus at two.

title: Agendando o jantar
grammar: On com dias e datas
reading: Nora is at home.
There is a calendar on the desk.
Saturday is busy, but Friday is free.
Nora and Lee are friends.
Dinner is on Friday at seven.
It is time for a hot drink!
dialogue: Hi, Lee! Are you free this week? It is time for dinner!
Hmm, my calendar is full. Saturday is busy.
Really? Is Friday free? What is the date?
Friday is free, yes. The date is June twelve.
Perfect! Dinner is on Friday at seven.
Great. Is the place near the station?
Yes, it is. Go straight, and it is by the old sign.
Okay, dinner on Friday. See you there, and I am on time!

title: Um passeio antes do anoitecer
grammar: Before e after antes de um horário ou evento
reading: It is evening, and the sun is low.
The sunset is at seven.
Ella and Sam go for a walk in the park.
The dog is with them.
The evening is cold, so they take a jacket.
After the walk, they read a book and sleep.
dialogue: It is a nice evening, Sam. Please come to the park with me.
Sure! Is the park near your apartment?
Yes, it is. The sunset is at seven, so go before dark.
Good idea. I read a book before dinner, so I am free.
Wonderful. Take a jacket, because the evening is cold.
OK. After dinner I sleep, so I am ready now.
Is it time to go for a walk? Do not run, and stay on the path.
Yes, we are on time. It is before dark. See you at the park!

title: Uma mesa para duas pessoas
grammar: For para indicar para quem ou para quantas pessoas
reading: Chris and Pat are at a restaurant.
It is a busy night.
There is no reservation.
The server is at the desk.
There is a small table by the window.
A menu and some water are on the table.
dialogue: Good evening! Is there a reservation for tonight?
No, there is not. Is there a small table for two?
Yes, there is. Is it a party of two?
Yes, it is. It is Friday at half past six.
Great. Please take the table near the window.
Thank you. Can I have a menu and some water, please?
Sure, here you are. Please speak to me if you need more.
Perfect, thank you. This table for two is nice.

title: Na sala de aula
grammar: Perguntas sobre posse com do e have
reading: It is a new school year.
Omar is in the classroom.
He is at a small desk by the window.
There is a notebook on the desk.
The pencil is not here.
Lia is next to Omar.
dialogue: Hi, Omar! Is this desk free?
Yes, it is. Sit here, next to me.
Thanks. It is a nice classroom.
Yes. What time is the class on Friday?
It is at nine, so we are on time. Oh no, I do not have a pencil!
No problem. I have two pencils. Here you are.
Thank you! Do you have an eraser, too?
Yes, I do. Here you go.

title: Pagando com cartão
grammar: Perguntas de sim ou não com can
reading: I am Leo, and I am at a small store.
My mother and father are at a table by the door.
There is a card reader on the desk.
I have no cash today.
I would like to pay by card.
The receipt is on the desk.
dialogue: Hello! That is eight dollars. Do you have cash or a card?
I do not have cash. Can I pay by card, please?
Yes, you can. Put your card in the card reader.
Okay, here it is. Is the card reader on?
Yes, it is. Please wait a minute.
No problem. Can I have a receipt, too?
Sure. Here is your receipt, and thank you.
Thank you! It is easy to pay by card.

title: Esperando na sala de atendimento
grammar: Can e cannot para permissões
reading: I am in the waiting room.
My sister is with me, and my brother is at work.
I am a patient here, and some people have cash or a card.
There is a sign by the door.
You can wait here, but you cannot run.
The nurse is at the desk.
dialogue: Good morning! Please take a seat in the waiting room.
Thank you. Can I wait here, near the door?
Yes, you can. Please wait, and the doctor is next.
Okay. My sister is in the car. Is there a chair for her, too?
Yes, there is. It is next to the table. Do not run, please.
Sure, no problem. Is there some water here?
Yes, there is water by the desk. But you cannot use a phone here.
Okay, I understand. Thank you!

title: Perguntando sobre a volta
grammar: Can we…? para perguntar por uma opção conjunta
reading: Rob and May are at the ticket desk in the city.
They are brother and sister, and it is a family trip.
They would like a round trip, not one way.
The fare is low, and they have money.
The return train is at six.
They come back on Sunday.
dialogue: Hello! Can we buy a round-trip ticket to Chicago, please?
Sure. Is it for Friday?
Yes, it is. Is there a return train on Sunday evening?
Yes, there is. It is at six. The fare is forty dollars.
That is fine. Can we pay by card?
Of course. Do you have a card, or do you have cash?
We have a card. Can we come back on Monday, too?
Yes, you can. Here are your tickets. Thank you!

title: A rotina no computador
grammar: Presente simples com I para falar de rotina
reading: I come to the classroom at eight.
I sit at my desk and open the computer.
The screen is blue, and I type my name on the keyboard.
I check my email before class.
I open a green folder on the screen.
Then I wait for the teacher.
dialogue: Hi Ben, is this your computer?
Yes, it is. I use it every day.
Can I look at the screen? It is blue.
Sure. I check my email here before class.
Do you have a mouse for this computer?
Yes, I have one. Here you are.
Thanks. Can I type my name on the keyboard?
Yes, you can. Please sit at my desk, and wait.

title: Organizando o material de estudo
grammar: He e she com a terminação -s no presente
reading: Mia sits at her study desk every day.
She uses a notebook for English.
Her brother Tom uses a planner.
He writes the date on every page.
Tom uses the computer screen and the keyboard.
Mia is tired, but she is happy.
dialogue: Noah, is this Mia's study desk?
Yes, it is. She uses a planner every day.
Nice. I use a notebook and my computer.
Her brother Tom types on the keyboard and looks at the screen.
Do you have a pencil? I want to write a note.
Yes, I have one. Here you are.
Thanks. Is Mia happy with her study desk?
Yes, she is. She studies there every day.

title: Estudando em grupo
grammar: We e they ao relatar o que grupos fazem
reading: Today we work outdoors at school.
I am in group one with Rosa and Tom, my classmates.
We sit at a big table under a tree.
They work together on a computer.
We are hungry, but we wait for lunch.
At two, both groups take a seat and share their work.
dialogue: Are we in the same group, Noah?
Yes, we are. We work together on page two.
Great. Where are our classmates this morning?
They are under that tree, near the big table.
Do they have a computer? We need a screen.
Yes, they have one. They wait for us.
Good. Please take a seat. We are hungry.
Yes, we are. We can eat after school.

title: Chegando com a mala
grammar: Afirmativas com have e has
reading: Sam and Liz are at the station with their luggage.
Sam has a big suitcase, and it is heavy.
Liz has a small carry-on bag.
It is cold, and Sam has a new coat in his suitcase.
Liz has a computer and a planner in her bag.
They go to the beach, and they help each other.
dialogue: Hi Rosa! Is this your suitcase?
Yes, it is. I have a heavy suitcase.
Wow. Can I help you with the luggage?
Thanks. Do you have a carry-on bag too?
Yes, I have a small bag with my computer and planner.
Good. It is cold today. Do you have a coat?
No, but Mia has a new coat in her bag.
Great. Yes, we can go to the beach now.

title: O horário de fechamento do parque
grammar: What time does…? com verbos de funcionamento
reading: It is late, and Ana and Noah are outdoors in the park.
A sign by the gate shows the closing time.
The park closes at six, so they walk on the pathway.
Noah wants a hot drink before it closes.
A group of people comes to the park every day.
At six, a man says, “Please close the gate.”
dialogue: Excuse me. What time does the park close?
It closes at six. Now it is five thirty.
Only thirty minutes! Can we walk outdoors now?
Yes, we can. Is there a hot drink near the gate?
Yes, there is a small cafe. A group goes there every day.
Nice. What time does the cafe close?
At six too, I think. Can we have a hot drink?
Yes, we can. It is a good plan.

title: Quantos minutos até o lago?
grammar: How long para perguntar pela duração
reading: Ida and Leo are at the park entrance.
They want to see the lake before it closes.
A sign shows the closing time and the lake path.
The walking time is short: the lake is ten minutes away.
They walk on the pathway, and the water is near.
Soon they sit on a bench by the water.
dialogue: Excuse me. Is this the way to the lake?
Yes, it is. Walk on the pathway.
Thanks. How long does it take to walk there?
It takes ten minutes. Please read the sign here.
OK. The sign says the closing time is six.
Yes. Can we walk to the lake before it closes?
Sure. Is there a bench by the water?
Yes, there is. It is a nice place.

title: Confirmando a plataforma
grammar: Which para escolher entre opções
reading: Pablo and Nina are at the station with a heavy suitcase.
There are three platforms, and the night train arrives soon.
Pablo has the tickets, but Nina has the luggage.
They ask a woman, “Which platform is for this train?”
She says, “Platform two, track four.”
They walk to platform two, and the train arrives in one minute.
dialogue: Excuse me. Which platform is for the night train?
Platform two. It arrives in five minutes.
Thank you. Which track is it? My suitcase is heavy.
Track four, near the big sign on the left.
Sorry, can you speak slowly, please?
Sure. Platform two, track four. Wait near the stairs.
Thanks. Is the night train on platform two now?
Yes, it is. It arrives in one minute.

title: Tomando notas para a aula
grammar: In e on para localizar o que foi escrito
reading: Kim sits at a desk with a pen and a heavy notebook.
She wants to take notes in class.
She writes the new word in her notebook.
The date goes on the first page, with the year.
Her birthday is on Friday, so she writes it in the notebook.
After a minute, she reads her notes on the train.
dialogue: Tom, where can I write the new word?
Write it in your notebook, Kim.
OK. And the date? The library closes soon.
Put the date on the first page. Then write the year.
Can I take notes with your pen, please?
Sure. Here you are. Your train arrives in a minute.
Thanks. Can I write my birthday in your notebook?
Yes, you can. Please write it now.

title: Informando o nome na recepção
grammar: Under + nome em uma reserva
reading: Ana walks into a hotel with her heavy suitcase.
She wants to check in at the front desk.
The hotel clerk asks, “What name is the reservation under?”
Ana says, “It is under my name, Ana Silva.”
The clerk gives her a pen and one page.
Then she gives Ana a room key.
dialogue: Hello! Are you here to check in?
Yes, I have a reservation for two nights.
What name is the reservation under, please?
It is under my name, Ana Silva.
Yes, I see it. Is your mother here too?
Yes, my mother and father are in the car.
Good. Take this pen, write your name on the page, and take the key.
Thank you! Yes, I have the key and my suitcase.

title: Subindo de elevador
grammar: On + andar
reading: Mia and her sister Ana are at the hotel.
They check in at the front desk.
The hotel clerk gives Mia a key.
Her room is on the second floor.
Ana has a room on the first floor.
Mia pushes the button and the elevator comes.
dialogue: Hello, I want to check in under my name, Mia Lopes.
Welcome, Mia! Your room is on the second floor.
Great. Is the elevator near the front desk?
Yes, it is. Push the button and wait, please.
My sister has a room too. Is it on the second floor?
No, her room is on the first floor, near the lobby.
Really? Okay. I see the stairs. Can I use them?
Yes, you can. Here is your key, and have a nice day.

title: Lendo o número do assento
grammar: Ordinal para localizar assentos e fileiras
reading: Lia and her family take the train to the lake.
They arrive at platform two and get on.
Lia has a ticket for seat twelve.
Her seat is in the third row, by the window.
Her brother sits in the second row.
Lia looks at the number and smiles.
dialogue: Excuse me, I have a ticket for seat twelve.
Seat twelve is in the third row, by the window.
Thank you. Is my seat next to the door?
No, it is near the window. The first row is by the door.
Oh, I see the number now. My brother has seat eleven.
Seat eleven is in the second row, near your seat.
Okay. Can my brother and I sit together, please?
Yes, you can. Your family can sit together here.

title: Dizendo quando sai a próxima partida
grammar: The next + nome para identificar o próximo item
reading: Noah and his sister are at the station.
He looks at the display for the time.
The next train departs at three.
It is the red line, and it arrives at platform two.
A later train departs at four.
Noah and his sister wait there for the train.
dialogue: Excuse me, what time does the next train depart?
The next train departs at three. Look at the display.
Which line is it? I see the color red on the display.
It is the red line. It arrives at platform two.
Is there a later train? My sister wants to buy a snack.
Yes, there is. A later one leaves at four.
Great, we have time for a snack. Thank you!
No problem. Yes, the red line is at platform two.

title: Deixando um recado no papel
grammar: Please + verbo em recados
reading: Rosa is a hotel clerk at the front desk.
A man comes and wants to leave a message.
He takes a blue pen and a page of paper.
He writes his name and his phone number on the note.
The note says, "Please call back after six."
Rosa puts the note by the phone.
dialogue: Hello, Rosa. Can I leave a message for my friend?
Sure, Tom. Take a pen and write on this page.
What do I write on the page? I have his phone number.
Write this: Please call back after six.
Okay, I have the pen. Is blue fine for the note?
Yes, blue is fine. Please write your name big.
Done! Please give this note to my friend, Rosa.
Of course, Tom. The note is by the phone now.

title: Chegando cedo à clínica
grammar: Early, late e on time com be
reading: Iris has an appointment at the clinic at ten.
She is early today, and she is happy.
She takes the elevator to the second floor.
She checks in at the front desk.
The nurse says the doctor is not late.
Iris is tired, so she sits and waits.
dialogue: Hello, I want to check in. My appointment is at ten.
It is under your name. You are early, Iris.
Really? I am happy. Is the doctor on time today?
Yes, she is on time. Take the elevator to the second floor.
Good. I am tired, so I want to sit. Can I wait here?
Of course. Take a seat by the window. The nurse can call you.
Thank you. Can I call my sister on my phone?
Yes, you can. Please do not talk loud, okay?

title: Embarcando no trem
grammar: Must para uma obrigação simples
reading: Dan has a big bag and a ticket for the next train.
He is early, so he waits by the door.
The train stops, and the passengers get off.
Dan must wait for the passengers first.
Then he can board the train.
He puts his luggage by his seat in the third row.
dialogue: Excuse me, can I board the train now?
Not yet. The passengers must get off first.
Okay. Is this the next train on the display? I am early.
Yes, it is. Now you can board the train. Please use this door.
Do I show my ticket here? My luggage is big.
Yes, you must show your ticket at the door.
Here you are. Can I put my luggage by my seat?
Yes, you can. Your seat is in the third row.

title: Combinando uma caminhada
grammar: Would you like to + ação para convidar
reading: Jules wants to take a walk in the small park.
Ben is her walking partner.
She calls him in the morning.
They want to meet by the old tree.
They walk together and talk a lot.
Later, Ben has her phone number for the next walk.
dialogue: Hi, Ben! Would you like to walk with me?
Yes, I would. Where do you want to meet?
Can we meet in the park by the old tree?
Sure. Is it a small park or a big park?
It is a small park, and it is very nice.
Would you like to go early, at eight?
Eight is early for me. Can we walk together at nine?
Yes, nine is good. I have your phone number, Jules.

title: Mandando uma mensagem rápida
grammar: Present continuous para uma ação em andamento
reading: Ivan is outside the door, and it is cold.
He is typing a text message to Tess.
Tess is reading the new message on her phone.
She is sending a reply right now.
Tess types the next text and opens the door.
Later, they have hot tea in the kitchen.
dialogue: Hi, Tess! I am outside the door, and it is cold.
Oh no! I am reading your text message right now.
Good. Please send a reply, and then open the door.
I am sending my reply now. Wait a minute, Ivan.
Please hurry. My hands are cold, and I want to go in.
I am coming to the door right now.
Great! I am early, so I can wait here.
Yes, you are early. Come in, and have some hot tea.

title: Ligando para uma amiga
grammar: Who para perguntar pela identidade
reading: Ana wants to call her friend Kim after school.
She uses her phone, and it rings two times.
A man answers, and she hears his voice.
Ana says her name and asks for Kim.
Kim is at home, and she comes to the phone.
Then the two friends talk about the park.
dialogue: Hello? Who is this, please?
This is Ana. Is Kim at home?
Yes, she is at home. Are you her friend?
Yes, I am her friend from school. I have a text message for her.
Wait a moment, please. She is in the kitchen.
Thank you. I want to meet her at the park later.
Hello, Ana! This is Kim. Can we meet right now?
Yes, we can. Please reply to my text message, Kim.

title: Um café antes de voltar para casa
grammar: And e but para juntar duas ideias simples
reading: Tina and her friend Lou go to a coffee shop.
Tina has a cup of coffee and a cookie.
Lou is tired, but he wants to read a book.
He wants to go home and sleep.
Tina says he can stay a little longer.
They sit at a table and talk about their walk.
dialogue: Do you want a cup of coffee, Lou?
Yes, please. A cookie too, please.
Sure. Take the table by the window. I have a text message to read.
Thank you. I want to stay, but I want to go home soon.
Can you stay a little longer? My friend is early, and she wants to meet you.
Okay, I can stay. You talk to her, and I read my book.
Good. You are tired, so please sit here with me.
Yes, I am tired. I sit here with my cup of coffee.

title: Geladeira vazia na cozinha
grammar: Some e any em frases e perguntas
reading: Mia opens the fridge, and it is almost empty.
There is some yogurt and one orange.
There isn't any butter, and there aren't any tomatoes.
Tom looks at the stove, and then at the oven.
"There are some noodles in the box," he says.
Mia says, "I cook, and you wash the dishes."
dialogue: Tom, I am hungry. What is in the fridge?
Not much. I see some yogurt and one orange.
Is there any chocolate? I want something sweet.
No chocolate, sorry. But I see an onion and a carrot.
Hmm. The market across the bridge is open now.
Okay. I can go there. What do we need?
Please buy some noodles and some butter.
Sure, no problem. I go now, and you wait here.

title: Feriado de fim de ano
grammar: Meses e datas (December twenty-fifth)
reading: December is the last month of the year.
Christmas is on December twenty-fifth.
New Year's Eve is on December thirty-first.
Mia sends a holiday card with a stamp from the post office.
In winter, the town has beautiful lights.
At midnight on New Year's Eve, there are fireworks!
dialogue: Mia, what is the date today?
It is December thirteenth, and winter is here.
What day is the holiday party at school?
It is on December twentieth, at six in the evening.
Great! I need a small gift, maybe a shirt, for my uncle.
Me too. A nice scarf is thirteen dollars. Thanks for the idea!
You are welcome. And New Year's Eve is December thirty-first, right?
Yes, it is. We can watch the fireworks from my window.

title: Procurando o guarda-chuva perdido
grammar: Pronomes possessivos (mine, yours, his, hers)
reading: It is a rainy day, and Rosa is at the airport lost and found.
A clerk puts three things on the desk: a purse, gloves, and a watch.
Rosa sees her wallet, and it is hers.
Her passport is inside, and her umbrella is there too.
Her brother Leo is with her, and he sees his jeans and his glasses.
The jeans are his, and the glasses are his too.
dialogue: Hello! Can I help you? Do you need something?
Yes, please. I'm looking for a small brown wallet. It has a card.
I see one here. Is this your wallet? Look inside, please.
Yes, it is. This wallet is mine! Thank you so much.
You're welcome. What about this watch? Is it yours?
No, it's not mine. It's his, I think. He's with me.
Okay. And look at this red umbrella. It's wet from the rain and the wind.
Oh, yes! That's my umbrella, and now I'm ready for the rain.

title: Show de mágica no teatro infantil
grammar: Where e when em perguntas simples
reading: The kids are at the theater for a magic show.
The magician has a long cape with a gold star.
He has a wand, and he can do a trick with a hat.
He puts a rabbit in a basket, but it is not a trap.
He opens an umbrella, and the rabbit jumps out of it.
The kids laugh, and they love the surprise.
dialogue: Mom, when is the magic show? Is it now?
No, it starts at three. It is at the theater, in the big room.
Where is the magician? I can't see him yet.
He is near the curtain. Look, he is coming out now!
Wow! I love his big wand.
It is in his hand. Watch him do a trick with the rabbit.
Look, the basket is empty! Where is the rabbit?
Here it is, on his arm! What a surprise, Noah!

title: Pizza por telefone
grammar: Partitivos (a slice of, a bottle of, a piece of)
reading: It is movie night, and Ana is at home with her cousin Leo.
They have popcorn, but they are still hungry.
Ana calls the pizza place and asks for delivery.
She would like half and half. One topping is ham, and the other topping is cheese.
The delivery driver is here, and the pizza has a lot of sauce.
Leo has pizza on his pants, and the two cats are happy!
dialogue: Hello, Pizza Palace. What would you like?
Hi! I would like one large pizza for delivery, please.
Sure. Is it half and half?
Yes, it is. Ham on one side and cheese on the other side.
Nice. Can I add a bottle of water for you?
Yes, please. And can I have a slice of cake?
Sure. There is also a piece of garlic bread for movie night, and the sauce is free.
Great, that is all. Thank you very much!

title: Ônibus pela cidade
grammar: By + transporte (by bus, by car)
reading: Tom is a commuter, and he goes downtown by bus.
His route is long, and there is a lot of traffic.
Today the bus is crowded, and Tom is near the door.
The driver is nice, but this trip is slow.
At Main Street, Tom has a transfer to Bus 5.
Tom says, "Get off here!" He is late, and his face is red.
dialogue: Hi, Tom! Are you here for the bus?
Yes, I am. I go downtown by bus, and it is a long route.
Really? I go by taxi, and the driver is very nice.
A taxi is nice, but the traffic is bad. The bus is slow today.
Look, here is the bus. Do not miss it!
Wow, it is crowded! Can you see a seat?
Yes, there is a seat behind the driver. Sit there, and put on your seatbelt.
Thanks. Is there a transfer at Main Street?
Yes, there is. Take Bus 5, and get off here at Pine Street.
Great, that is clear. Thank you, Mia!

title: Abastecendo no posto
grammar: Too e very com adjetivos
reading: Rosa is at the gas station with her car.
The tank is empty, and she says, "Fill it up, please."
The pump is very old, but it works.
The price is too high today.
The hose is too short, and the car is too far.
Rosa can run inside to pay, and she is very happy.
dialogue: Good afternoon! Pump number three is free.
Thanks. Fill it up, please. The tank is very empty.
Sure. Regular fuel or premium?
Regular, please. Wow, the price is too high today!
Yes, it is. Gas is expensive this week.
That is too much money! And my route is very long today.
I know. Is your tent in the car? You need a flashlight and a lot of gas for camping.
True. Please check the tires, and clean the window.
No problem. It is done, and the tank is full now.
Perfect, it is full. Thank you!

title: Domingo na pista de skate
grammar: Every + período (every morning, every Sunday)
reading: Every Sunday, Ben and Mia go to the skate park.
Ben has a skateboard, and he always has his knee pads.
The ramp is big, and the sky is blue.
Ben can ride fast, but the ramp is a little scary.
"Do not skip the knee pads!" says Mia.
After the park, they have pizza.
dialogue: Hey, Ben! Are you ready for the ramp today?
Yes, I am. I come here every Sunday morning.
Me too! I skate here every morning with my dad.
Every morning? Wow, I am tired every day!
Look, I can jump now! Watch me.
Nice jump! Be safe, and put on your knee pads.
Ouch! I fall on the ramp, and my tooth hurts a little, but I am okay.
Good. The ramp is scary, but it is fun.
Yes! After skating, can we order a pizza for delivery?
Sure, that is a great idea!

title: Colegas de trabalho novos
grammar: Be + adjetivo de personalidade com very e really
reading: Rosa has a new colleague, and his name is Noah.
Noah is very funny, and he has a big smile.
Lia is shy, but she is really smart and kind.
At the meeting, they are all polite.
Rosa and Noah are in the same soccer league on Saturday.
They get along well, and Rosa is happy.
dialogue: Hi, Rosa! How is your new job?
It is great! My new colleagues are really nice.
Really? Tell me about them. Who is Noah?
Noah is very funny. He is big and strong, and he plays in a soccer league.
And the woman near the window? Is she nice too?
That is Lia. She is shy, but she is really smart.
Great! So you get along well with them, right?
Yes, we do. We eat together in the kitchen at lunch.
That is nice. Is your route to work easy now?
Yes, it is. I have one transfer, and I am a happy commuter.

title: Jogo de futebol
grammar: Play e go + esporte (play soccer, go running)
reading: Lia and Noah play soccer on Saturday.
Noah is on a team with his colleague Tom.
The field is big, and the day is hot.
Noah can kick the ball very hard.
He can score a goal, and the team can win.
After the game, they stop at the gas station for water.
dialogue: Hi, Noah! Can you play soccer with us today?
Yes, I can! I play soccer on Saturday and tennis on Sunday.
Great. The game is at the field near the school, and it is hot today.
No problem. I go to the field by skateboard, and I have water.
Funny! My colleague Tom goes running before the game, so he is ready.
Cool. Can I kick the ball first, please?
Sure. Kick it hard, and try to score a goal.
Look, I score a goal! Is it good?
Yes, great goal! Now our team can win today.
Yes, we can win! Who has the water?

title: Escolhendo tênis
grammar: Superlativos (the best, the cheapest)
reading: Ana and her colleague Ben are at a shoe store, and there is snow outside.
Ana wants a pair of sneakers for tennis.
The blue sneakers are the cheapest.
The black sneakers are the best, and they are light.
The laces are white, and the price is fifty dollars.
They are expensive, but Ana likes them.
dialogue: Do you like these sneakers for tennis, Ana?
Yes, I do. They are the best in the store.
Really? The sandals are cheap here, and they look cool.
I know, but I need shoes for soccer with my team.
Okay. Are the boots good for soccer?
No, they aren't. They are the heaviest in the store.
Then try the black sneakers. They are the lightest.
Oh, they are very comfortable, and the laces are white!
Great! Is the price fifty dollars?
Yes, it is. Let's pay and then eat a snack.

title: Inverno na cabana
grammar: In + estação e it gets + adjetivo
reading: Rosa and Noah are in a cabin in winter.
It gets very cold, and there is snow outside.
Noah puts wood on the fire.
The fireplace is big, and the room gets warm fast.
Rosa has a scarf, gloves and a pair of boots.
Her feet are cold, and she wants to warm up.
dialogue: It is cold in winter here. Come to the fireplace, Rosa!
Thanks! My feet are wet from the snow.
Take off your boots, and put them near the fire.
Good idea. I have a sweater in my bag, and a scarf too.
In the morning, it gets very cold in this cabin.
Really? Then I need my gloves, and I need to warm up!
I have hot cocoa for you. It is on the table.
Wonderful! Does your puppy like the cabin in winter?
Yes, he does. He sleeps next to the fireplace all day.
Great! Now everyone is warm, and the cabin is nice.

title: Aula de dança
grammar: Advérbios de modo (well, fast, slowly)
reading: Lia is a dancer on a dance team.
Today she has a lesson on the stage.
Her teacher says, "Move slowly and feel the rhythm."
Lia can jump high, and she spins fast.
Max wears sneakers, and he dances fast.
They warm up first, and then they dance together.
dialogue: Max, your feet are fast, but the music is slow.
Oh, sorry! I want to be a good dancer on the stage.
Then listen to this rhythm. Dance slowly, and move your feet.
Like this? I can jump, but I cannot spin well.
No problem. Look at that teacher, and step to the beat.
She is a great dancer. She always steps to the beat.
Yes, she is. Do you warm up before the lesson?
Yes, I do. I run and move my arms first.
Good! Now try again, and listen to the beat.
Look, I spin well now. I can do it!

title: Passeio com a câmera
grammar: How about + verbo com -ing para sugerir
reading: Kim and Dan are at the zoo on a sunny day.
Kim has a camera, and Dan has a tripod.
Kim wears sneakers, and Dan wears boots.
They want a selfie with the tigers.
Dan says, "How about taking a photo here?"
Kim smiles, and Dan presses the button.
dialogue: Kim, how about taking a selfie by the tigers?
Good idea! Where is my camera, Dan?
It is in your bag, and I have a tripod too.
Great. How about putting the camera on the tripod?
Okay. Strike a pose, and say cheese, please!
Cheese! Is my smile good, or is it too small?
It is very good. Your scarf looks great in the photo.
Thanks! Now let's take a tour of the zoo.
Sure. How about walking to the monkeys first?
Yes, that is a great plan!

title: Videochamada com a equipe
grammar: Present continuous negativo e perguntas (I'm not, Are you?)
reading: Noah is at home, and he has a meeting at nine.
He sits at his laptop and puts on a headset.
His webcam is on, but the signal is weak.
Mia is in a cabin with her puppy.
The puppy wants pet food, and he is loud.
Noah says, "Mia, you're on mute!"
dialogue: Hi, Mia! Can you join the meeting now?
Yes, I can. I have my laptop and my headset here.
Great. Are you using your webcam today?
No, I'm not using it. The signal is weak in my cabin.
Hmm, I cannot hear you. Is your microphone working?
Yes, it is. Can you hear me now?
No, I can't. Wait, you're on mute!
Oh, sorry! Is this loud? My puppy is big, and he is very noisy.
Ha! Tell him to sit, and let's start.
Okay, he sits now, and I am ready for the meeting.

title: Revisão: Dia de mudança
grammar: Revisão: have to, can, there is/are e preposições de lugar
reading: Tom and Ana have a big moving day.
The truck is in front of the apartment, near a tree.
They have to carry the furniture upstairs.
There are many boxes, and the tape is on the table.
The sofa is next to the door, and the lamp is behind it.
Ana has her camera, and she wants a photo of the new kitchen.
dialogue: The truck is here, Ana. We have to carry the furniture upstairs.
Okay. Where does the sofa go?
There is a place between the window and the lamp. The wall has new paint.
Good. The bed is very heavy. Can you help me, please?
Sure. Let's try! You have to hold it on the left.
Okay. Where is the tape? I have to close this box.
It is on the kitchen table, next to the brush.
Here it is! There are two mirrors in this box. Can you take them?
Yes, I can. I put them behind the sofa for now.
Perfect! Everything is in the right place now.

title: Consertando o carro na oficina
grammar: Adjetivo + enough (big enough, hot enough)
reading: Ben has a brown truck.
The truck is old, but it is big enough for his boxes.
Today the engine is very loud.
Ben takes the truck to a mechanic.
The mechanic opens the hood and looks at the engine.
The brake is not good enough, so he repairs it.
dialogue: Hi, Mr. Cruz. My brown truck is very loud today.
Really? Please open the hood. I want to see the engine.
Sure. Here you are. Is the engine bad?
No, the engine is fine. But the brake is not good enough.
Oh no. Can you repair it today? I have an order for a customer.
Yes, I can. I have the tool, and the truck is not too damaged.
Great. Please change the oil, too. Is five o'clock late enough for you?
Yes, it is. Please bring the truck back at five.

title: Trilha na montanha
grammar: How far + distância (How far is it?)
reading: Mia and Ben are on a mountain trail.
The air is cool, and a bird sings near the river.
There is a written sign by the rock: two miles.
Mia asks, "How far is the hill?"
It is only one mile, so they climb up.
At the top, they eat a sausage and see a big field.
dialogue: Ben, look at the mountain! Is that the top?
Yes, it is. How far is it from here?
I press the button on my phone. It says three miles.
Three miles? Is that far?
No, it is not far. Our truck is by the river, and the air is cool.
Okay. I have a sausage and some water. How far is the hill?
The hill is near, only one mile. Then we climb up the rock.
Great. Well done, Mia. Let's go!

title: Casamento no domingo
grammar: Our e their
reading: Today is Rosa and Leo's wedding, and we are at the party.
Rosa is the bride, and Leo is the groom.
Her wedding dress is white, and his tie is green.
Their garden is lovely, and the flowers grow fast.
Our gift is on their table, next to the cake.
The music starts, and they kiss and dance.
dialogue: Look at the bride! Her wedding dress is beautiful.
Yes, it is. And the groom is very happy.
Where is our gift? I do not see it.
It is on their table, by the cake.
Good. Is dinner steak or chicken?
Steak, at six. Their friends from the mountain are here with a truck.
Listen, the music is loud. Do you want to dance?
Yes, I want to dance with you. Let's go!

title: Brinquedos na loja
grammar: How old + idade (He is six years old)
reading: Tom and his son Max are in a toy store.
Max is a boy, and he is six years old.
He likes the red truck, the big ball, and the kite.
His sister Lia is nine years old, and she wants a doll.
The girl and the boy enjoy the puzzle and the robot.
Then they pay for the doll, the truck, and the puzzle.
dialogue: Dad, look at this red truck! Can I have it?
Nice, but how old are you, Max?
I am six years old, Dad. I am big!
The box says it is for big kids, sorry.
Oh no. Then I want the puzzle. We can play with it together.
Good idea. And Lia wants the doll with a wedding dress.
Is the doll a bride? How old is she?
Yes, she is a bride! She is a toy, so she is not old. Let's pay.

title: Voo de balão
grammar: From + lugar + to + lugar
reading: Lia and Dan are in a hot air balloon.
They fly from the village to the mountain.
The balloon goes up, and the ground gets small.
The sky is blue, and there is a white cloud.
The flame makes the air hot, so they fly high.
Then they land next to a hill and a big rock.
dialogue: Wow! We are in the sky! Look at the ground.
It is so small! The cars are very small.
Where do we go next?
We fly from the village to the mountain.
The flame is small. Please pull the rope.
Okay. Now we fly higher. Look, there is a cloud!
It is big and white. Then we land near the hill, right?
Yes, from the village to the hill. Then we land next to a rock.

title: Escada rolante no metrô
grammar: Into, out of, up e down para movimento
reading: Ben and Ana are in the subway.
They go down the escalator and into the train.
A voice says, "Mind the gap!"
A bride in a wedding dress sits near the door.
At the museum, they get out of the train and find the exit.
They go up the escalator, and the sky is gray with a big cloud.
dialogue: Ben, which exit is for the museum?
I do not know. I am a visitor here, too.
Look at the map. First we go down the escalator, then into the train.
Okay. Mind the gap! It is rush hour, so the train is full.
Hurry! I have an exam at nine. This is a good example of a bad morning!
Ha! Look, the bride in the wedding dress is by the pole.
Great. After the tunnel, we get out of the train and go up.
Yes, we go up the escalator, and the museum is there.

title: Revisão: Faxina em casa
grammar: Revisão: frequência, why/because, present continuous e how much/many
reading: Rosa cleans her house every Saturday.
Today she is using a vacuum in the living room.
A few toys, dolls, and puzzles are on the floor.
She is tidying up because the room is very dirty.
She puts the trash in a bucket.
Soon the room is clean, and the kids are happy.
dialogue: Rosa, why are you using the vacuum so early?
Because my sister is coming at ten. I always clean on Saturday.
How many rooms are you cleaning today?
Three. I use a mop in the kitchen and a broom in the hall.
How much dust is there under the bed?
A lot! Please bring the broom and the bucket.
Sure. I have a few bags for the trash, too.
Yes, that is perfect. Thank you!

title: Praça de alimentação
grammar: Too e also para acrescentar (me too, I also like)
reading: Ben and his sister Lia are at the food court.
It is near the escalator to the subway exit.
Ben likes a burger with fries.
Lia likes a burger too.
She also likes soda, and her straw is red.
Her tray is full, and Ben's tray is full too.
dialogue: Hi! I'd like a burger and fries, please.
Sure, it is your turn. Is it to eat here or to go?
To eat here. My sister wants a burger too.
Okay. Two burgers and two fries. Anything else?
Yes, one soda for me. She also likes soda.
Really? Then two sodas. Here is your tray.
Thanks. Where is the ketchup? I like it on fries.
It is next to the salt, near the straws.
Great. Is there onion on this burger? I like onion too.
Yes, there is onion. Enjoy your burger!

title: Bombeiros na rua
grammar: Someone, everyone e nobody
reading: Today there is a fire in a small house.
The alarm is loud, and someone calls for help.
A siren comes closer, and the firefighters arrive.
One firefighter wears a hard hat and holds the hose.
Another one climbs the ladder to the window.
Soon the smoke is gone, and everyone is safe.
dialogue: Look! I see smoke and fire in that house.
Oh no! Is someone inside the house right now?
I don't know. Call for help now, please!
Okay. Hello? There is a fire. Please send an ambulance.
Listen! I hear a siren, and the firefighters are here.
Good. They have a ladder and a long hose.
Is everyone out? I see nobody at the windows.
Look! A firefighter with a hard hat is on the ladder.
Be careful. There is a wire on the road near the tire.
Great news! Everyone is safe now, and we can have a soda.

title: Revisão: Parque de diversões
grammar: Revisão: comparativos, superlativos, how old, can e too/very
reading: Mia and her brother Noah are at the amusement park.
The roller coaster is the tallest ride, and the carousel is slower.
The pirate ship is a bit scary, but the roller coaster is very scary.
Noah is eight years old, so he can ride the swing.
At a game, a clown gives Mia a prize, a toy sheep.
They laugh a lot and eat burgers with soda.
dialogue: The roller coaster is the tallest ride here!
Yes, it is taller than the pirate ship.
Is it scary? I am only eight years old.
A bit. The carousel is not scary, and it is slower.
Okay. Can I go on the swing too?
Sure. Look, a clown has a game with a big prize.
Cool! The toy sheep is the best prize.
It is cute, but the game is harder than it looks.
Look, I have the sheep! I can laugh now, and I am hungry.
Yes, you have the best prize. Now we can eat fries.

title: Corrida de rua
grammar: Be going to em negativas e perguntas
reading: Lia is a runner, and today is a long race.
She has light shoes and a bottle of water.
Her friends are not going to run, but they are going to cheer.
Ready, set, go! The race starts.
Lia is not going to stop, and she runs to the finish.
She is going to get a medal, and everyone is happy.
dialogue: Are you going to run in the race today?
Yes, I am. It is a long race, but I am ready.
I am not going to run. I am going to cheer for you.
Thanks! Can you hold my water bottle, please?
Sure. Are you going to wear those shoes? They look light.
Yes, my new shoes are light, and my legs feel strong.
Look, the runners are at the line. Ready, set, go!
See you at the finish! Look for me near the clown.
Okay. After the race, we can have a soda and sit on a bench.
Yes, and the winner gets a prize. Good luck!

title: Chamando o encanador
grammar: Passado negativo com didn't
reading: Rosa has a leak in her kitchen.
There is a puddle and a spider under the sink.
She puts a bucket under the old pipe.
The plumber looked at it and used a big wrench.
He fixed the pipe, but he didn't fix the sink.
He didn't have the right tool.
dialogue: Hello! Are you the plumber? I have a leak in my kitchen.
Yes, I am. Is the leak under the sink?
Yes, it is. There is a drip from the pipe and a big puddle.
Wow, that is a lot of water. Do you have a bucket and a towel?
Yes, I do. I didn't see it at first, but now it is very big.
OK. Let me look at the pipe. Oh, there is a spider here too!
Really? I don't like spiders. On my uncle's farm, they live in the barn.
Don't worry. I can fix the sink today, but I didn't bring the new part.
Oh no. So you can't fix it now?
Right. I can stop the leak now, and I'm coming back tomorrow with the new part.

title: Lembranças do show
grammar: Did em perguntas de passado
reading: Ben and Mia were at a concert in the park.
The band played a new song.
The drums were very loud.
The crowd clapped and danced.
Everybody wanted to sing along.
Ben loved the music, and Mia loved the singer.
dialogue: Hi Ben! Did you go to the concert at the park?
Yes, I did! My sister Mia and I loved it.
Really? Did you like the band? I want to hear all about it.
Yes, I did. They played a new song, and the drums were very loud.
Cool! Was the crowd big? Was it like a sold-out show at the theater?
Yes, it was! The audience clapped, and everybody wanted to sing along.
Did you sing along too? Would you like to show me the song?
Sure. I can't sing well, but I can play the music on my phone.
Could you play it again, please? I like the drums.
Sure. Here you are! Yes, the band is great.

title: Show de talentos na escola
grammar: Passado irregular 1 (went, had, ate, saw)
reading: Noah went to the school talent show with Rosa.
A boy had a funny joke, and the audience laughed.
The judge saw a girl in a ghost costume.
She was the winner, and she had a big smile.
The judge said, "Clap your hands!"
Rosa and Noah ate pumpkin cookies after the show.
dialogue: Hi Noah! Did you like the talent show at school?
Yes, I did! I went with Rosa, and we had great seats.
Nice! Was the show long? I want to hear everything.
No, it was short, but it was fun. The jokes were very funny, and the audience laughed.
Ha! Was the judge happy too?
Yes, she was. She said, "Clap your hands!" and the crowd clapped.
Who was the winner?
A girl in a ghost costume! I met her after the show and saw her gift.
That is great! Is there a talent show next month?
Yes, there is. Come with us and bring a funny joke!

title: Revisão: Reencontro de turma
grammar: Revisão: was/were, -ed, irregulares e did
reading: Rosa went to her school reunion.
She saw her old friends, and they had lunch together.
Tom had his old yearbook, and they looked at every photo.
Everybody laughed at a funny memory.
Mia remembered a story about the school band.
At the end, everybody took a new photo.
dialogue: Tom! You look great. It is so good to see you again!
Hi Rosa! Come here and give me a hug.
Ha ha! Let's catch up. What do you do now?
I work with a plumber. We fix a leak or a pipe every day.
Cool! I went to a clay class in May and made a mug.
Nice! Do you remember our school band? You had real talent.
Yes, I do! We had a concert, and the crowd clapped at your joke.
Ha! That is a good memory. Look, I have my old yearbook here.
We look so young! Let's take a new photo after lunch.
Yes, let's do it! Lunch is ready now.

title: Notícias do jornal
grammar: Ontem e atrás no tempo (yesterday, last week, ago)
reading: Ben opened the newspaper yesterday.
The headline said, "Big storm at the island!"
A reporter was on the island two days ago.
She had breaking news about the storm.
The weather was bad last week, and the traffic was slow.
Now the weather is sunny, and the island is safe.
dialogue: Noah, did you see the newspaper yesterday?
Yes, I did. The headline was about a big storm.
Wow! A reporter was on the island two days ago.
Yes. She had breaking news on TV at night. The weather was terrible.
Was the traffic bad too?
Yes, it was. Cars waited in the rain for two hours.
Is there a sports page? Our team had a game last week. It was the best game of the year.
Yes, there is. They played well, and the crowd clapped.
Great! Let's catch up on the news tonight.
Yes, let's read the headline together at my house.

title: Mercado de pulgas
grammar: Passado e futuro juntos (I went, I'm going to)
reading: Mia went to a flea market with her dad.
She saw an antique lamp on a vendor's table.
The price was ten dollars, but Mia wanted a bargain.
The vendor said, "OK, eight dollars."
That was a good deal for Mia.
Now she is going to put the lamp in her room.
dialogue: Look, Ana! This is my new sweater from the flea market.
It is so nice! Was it cheap?
Yes, it was a bargain! The vendor wanted only five dollars.
Great! Is there anything else good there?
Yes! They sell antique lamps, mugs, and pots. I love the old lamp.
Did you buy the lamp?
No, I didn't. The price was too high. I'm going to ask for a good deal next week.
Good idea! I'm going to go with you. Every old thing has a story.
Great! We can go on Saturday morning.
Yes, I'm free on Saturday. We can have lunch there too.

title: Revisão: Festa de despedida
grammar: Revisão geral: presente, passado e going to
reading: Today is the farewell party for the English class.
The teacher is giving each student a certificate.
Ana went up and made a short speech.
"I'm proud of this class," she said.
"We had many lessons and made new friends."
"Please keep in touch," the teacher said.
dialogue: Ben, you look sad. Are you OK?
I'm fine, Ana. It is the last day of class, and I'm a little sad.
Me too. I remember our first lesson. I was so nervous!
Yes! Now we can write a postcard or a story in English.
True. The teacher is going to give each student a certificate, and then teach us a song.
Nice! Did you write your speech?
Yes, I did. It is short. I'm going to say thank you to everybody.
That is a nice idea. I'm proud of you! Can we take a picture together?
Sure! After that, we can keep in touch. Here is my number.
Yes, please! We can catch up at a reunion next year.

title: Revisão final: Planos para o ano
grammar: Revisão final: presente, passado e going to
reading: Lia has a big dream for next year.
She is going to learn more English.
Her goal is to travel and see many islands.
She wants a good job in the future.
Last year she was a student, and now she has a certificate.
Lia wants her dream to come true.
dialogue: Noah, what is your plan for the future?
I'm going to learn to drive next year. My goal is to buy a car.
Cool! I'm going to travel to an island like the one on my old postcard.
That sounds fun! Don't forget sunscreen. The weather is dry and sunny there.
Good idea. I want a job with travel too. My dream is a career as a reporter.
A reporter? You can write a headline for the newspaper!
Yes! And you? What career do you want?
I want to be a plumber. I fixed a pipe last year, and I loved it.
That is a great plan! Please keep in touch, and we can catch up next year.
Yes, we can. I hope our dreams come true!
